image_description: A close-up, side-profile view of a black assault rifle (resembling an FN FNC or similar variant) held by a person in military camouflage fatigues. The image focuses on the receiver, pistol grip, trigger guard, and the rear portion of the stock. A scope is mounted on top. The background is blurred, showing hints of green foliage and white structures.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Compact automatic firearm with characteristic profile of barrel receiver and stock aligned linearly.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible components (receiver, grip, stock hinge) align correctly along a linear axis typical of rifle mechanics.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Overall length is substantial with barrel comprising a significant portion of total length.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image is a tight crop focusing on the mid-section; the muzzle and full barrel length are outside the frame, making this untestable.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Matte black or dark gray finish.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The metal and polymer surfaces exhibit a consistent matte black/dark gray finish with appropriate specular highlights.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Metallic receiver housing firing mechanism with detachable box magazine inserted below.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The receiver is clearly defined. While the magazine itself is largely obscured by the holder's arm/gear, the magazine well geometry is visible and consistent with a detachable box magazine design.
The barrel extends out of the left side of the frame; the muzzle device is not visible.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Pistol grip collapsible or fixed stock and handguard surrounding barrel.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The pistol grip is clearly visible and structurally sound. The rear of the handguard and the stock attachment point are visible and appear mechanically correct.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Parkerized or anodized metal with polymer furniture.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Texture analysis shows distinct differences between the metallic receiver (harder reflections) and the polymer grip/stock (softer, textured surface), consistent with real-world materials.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Upper receiver has carrying handle or Picatinny rail for optics.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: A mounting rail system is visible on top of the receiver, supporting a mounted optical sight.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Distinguishing features include magazine well and ejection port.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The ejection port cover and latch mechanism are clearly visible on the right side of the receiver. The magazine well opening is visible behind the trigger guard.

selected_experts.reason: To verify the specific model details and ensure the object is correctly classified as an assault rifle rather than a generic toy or prop.
To check for edge bleeding between the complex mechanical parts of the gun and the background/clothing, ensuring sharp boundaries.
To verify the spatial relationship between the rifle, the hands holding it, and the background, ensuring no geometric melting or depth inconsistencies.
To assess overall texture consistency, lighting coherence, and detect any subtle generative noise or blur artifacts.

focus_areas: Mechanical integrity of the receiver and trigger group
Boundary sharpness between the rifle and the camouflage clothing
Consistency of material textures (metal vs. polymer vs. fabric)
Logical connection of the stock to the receiver
custom_prompts_for_reflector: Pay close attention to the interface between the pistol grip and the user's hand/clothing. AI often struggles with how fingers wrap around complex grips or how fabric deforms against hard objects. Verify that the ejection port details are mechanically plausible for the identified rifle type.
